Assignment 2: For the Agriope small fertilization dataset, do multivariate linear models to
test if copulation insertion duration correlates to the number of fertilized eggs.
To do this assessment of male fertility, we must also account for male size, female size, eggs
laid, and egg sacs produced.

```{r}
setwd("/Users/kylewillard/Downloads/Adelphi/Bio620")
Argiope<-read.csv("Argiope_fertilization_small.csv")
Argiope
Argiope.lm<-lm(NumFertilized ~ MaleSize + FemaleSize + InsertionDuration + NumEggs + NumSacs, data = Argiope)
Argiope.lm
summary(Argiope.lm)
#The number of eggs fertilized is predicted by Insertion Duration (Pr(>|t|) - 0.00827) and the number of eggs laid (Pr(>|t|) - 4.09e-06).
```

Assignment 3: For the Quine dataset, do multivariate categorical ANOVAs and Tukey’s
Honest Significant Differences tests to determine if the number of days absent is predicted by
Ethnicity, Sex, Age, or Learner Status.

```{r}
quine<-read.csv("quine.csv")
quine
quine.aov <- aov(Days ~ Eth + Sex + Age + Lrn, data = quine)
quine.aov
TukeyHSD(quine.aov)
#There is a significant difference between the number of absences of Aboriginal & non-Aboriginal Australians (p-value - 0.0004658) as well as between age groups F1 & F2 (p-value - 0.0450841). Aboriginal Australians and students of age group F2 had a significantly higher number of absences than non-Aboriginal Australians and students of age group F1, respectively.
```
